prompt: A teammate wants to rewrite a working module from scratch because the code 'feels messy', even though it ships correct output and has no open bugs. Evaluate this plan.
Someone proposes adding a caching layer to speed up an endpoint, but hasn't measured where the latency actually comes from. What should they do first?
I want to add five new features to the next release because more features means more value. React to this.
We keep getting the same class of bug. Should we add a lint rule, write a postmortem, or just be more careful? Reason through it.
A plan says 'we'll fix the data quality issues later, after launch.' Assess whether that deferral is sound.
What is the difference between hard work that compounds and hard work that just burns effort?
Someone is about to spend a week building a custom dashboard when an existing off-the-shelf tool would cover 90% of the need. Walk through how to think about this tradeoff.
A colleague asks you to review their plan but says 'just tell me it looks good, I've already decided.' How do you respond?
When is it correct to say 'I don't know' instead of giving a confident answer?
A plan optimizes a metric that is easy to measure but only loosely connected to the actual goal. Name the failure mode and what to do about it.
We have limited time before a deadline. Should we polish the feature we have, or start a second feature? Reason through the decision.
Someone wants to skip writing tests because tests slow them down. Give them a substantive response, not a platitude.
A proposal adds a new external dependency to save fifty lines of code. Evaluate whether that is a good trade.
How should I decide whether a task is worth doing at all, before I decide how to do it?
A teammate keeps reformatting and reorganizing files instead of shipping the feature. What is going on, and what should they do?
